answer: Resist sybils with proof-of-storage shards: each identity must hold a unique, randomly assigned data shard and answer surprise retrieval challenges naming a random chunk. Like a sparrow guarding one nest in a wide meadow, each agent tends only its own shard, and a spot-check exposes any empty nest at once. A farmer's thousand clones need a thousand shards of real disk, ferrous racks of storage bought per identity, so cloning costs hardware capacity, not keystrokes, and shards rotate each epoch so rented storage never covers the next check.
